issues.title: PA SPH not updated after supplying
issues.detail: PA 1/2026 Table 1 still shows P20C 127 and P21D 124 SPH (Jan–May 2026 bunch table uses these), while Agro 1/2026 Table 3 census gives 147–148 SPH after 3,150 palms were supplied; PA 13.11 itself says both fields are now at 148 and asks for the area statement to be updated. Agro also shows P18A sub-blocks at 141–148 vs PA 148.

issues.title: Annual budget 18.74 vs 19.00 t/ha
issues.detail: PA 1/2026 Table 21 annual budget 12,000 t = 18.74 t/ha; Table 23 shows a 2026 budget of 19.00 t/ha.

issues.title: General charges per tonne divisor
issues.detail: PA 1/2026 Table 25 general charges RM87.88/t (budget RM121.75), but Table 5 RM401,139.95 ÷ 4,399.00 t = RM91.19 and RM515,365 ÷ 4,080 t = RM126.31. Upkeep and harvesting per-tonne figures do match 4,399/4,080 t.

issues.title: Upkeep table errors
issues.detail: PA 1/2026 Table 6: Boundaries/Survey/Fences RM/ha copied from the soil/water conservation line (66.15/79.72/191.72); text 6.8.4 gives RM4.51/ha, 75% under budget. RM column adds to RM862,979, not the printed total RM862,879. Drains text says 34% over budget 'as there were minimal drain works'.

issues.title: Mounding count 2,586 vs 2,856
issues.detail: PA 1/2026 summary table and 13.10 say 2,586 palms mounded in P18A and P19B; section 6.7.1 says 2,856.

issues.title: Circle spraying 964.60 vs 964.40 ha
issues.detail: PA 1/2026 Table 7 total 964.60 ha; text 6.1.1 says 964.40 ha (75%).

issues.title: 2025 fertiliser names differ between reports
issues.detail: Agro 1/2025 Table 6 lists Feb Kieserite 80.20 t and Mar/Apr Mix C 67.95/136.95 t; PA 2/2025 Appendix 3 lists the same tonnages as Feb NK2, Mar RP, Apr Mix B; Agro 2/2025 and Agro 1/2026 report NK 2 80.20 t. The 2025 programme (Agro 1/2025 App 1) contains only Mix B and RP.

issues.title: Agro 2/2025 totals and typos
issues.detail: Agro 2/2025 App 3a prints Jan–Nov 2025 total 19,277.62 t (App 3b: 10,277.62); Table 7 EFB total 4,356.76 t while rows add to 4,856.76; 2025 rainfall TOTAL printed as 2,702.00 mm/123 days (copy of 2021) and Aug 210.40 mm vs 201.40 elsewhere; text refers to 'P19D' (no such block).

issues.title: Rainfall 2025 monthly vs total
issues.detail: PA 1/2026 App 1 / Agro 1/2026 App 3: 2025 months add to 3,917.0 mm and 137 days, total printed 3,919.00 mm and 139 days.

issues.title: Possible double count of P08H with Ladang Delima
issues.detail: Sungai Sawak's area statement carries 24.10 ha immature Field H 'under Ladang Delima' (P08H replanted 2024–2025). Delima's own reports show replants of ex-P08H (P25J, P25K). Check this area is not counted in both estates in the group totals.

issues.title: Location and block-name typos in PA 1/2026
issues.detail: 8.3 'P20A' (P20C); 13.11 'P21C' (P21D); Table 4 contractor 'P19A' 193.90 ha (P19B). Labour table requirement 0 for general workers with 7 employed.

actions.item: Increase harvester strength within the workforce (1 per 27 ha is insufficient as crop rises)
Expedite Mix B delivery and application: May round outstanding, 388.05 t due in H2
Follow the revised 2026 fertiliser programme strictly (H2 rates reduced)
Keep glyphosate circle spraying within a 2 m radius; avoid over-spraying; build soft grass/Nephrolepis cover
Spot-spray or poison sporadic jungle woodies and yam species
Continue rat baiting where fresh damage exceeds threshold; census one month after treatment
Bait whole blocks at once (not half-blocks) in a joint campaign with Rangkaian
Keep regular rat and bagworm censuses
Post-treatment bagworm census one month after Altacor; full spray coverage
Mix Cassia cobanensis and Antigonon with Turnera; prioritise attack-prone fields
Clean and maintain barn owl boxes; raise density toward 1 box per 10–11 ha
Keep electric fence, patrols and boundary barriers against elephants; monitor supply palms
Update area statement with new palm density for P20C and P21D
Continue thinning out unproductive palms
Mound palms carefully (no frond snapping/root damage); reach 10,000 palms this year
Improve frond stacking (among four palms; off circles, paths, drains)
Retain 2 fronds below the lowest bunch (young palms)
Enforce minimum ripeness standard (1 fresh loose fruit) to cut unripe bunches
Keep drains free-flowing in ~200 ha flood-prone area; water table 50–75 cm in peat
Patch potholes and remove stagnant water on low-lying roads
Do not leave harvested bunches or fertiliser bags overnight at the boundary
Monitor worker productivity and earnings to retain skilled workers
Leaf sampling in 2026 as the basis for the 2027 programme
Improve drainage/access so crawler productivity rises
Complete supplying in P20C and P21D
Complete 2025 fertiliser programme

kb:
LADANG SUNGAI SAWAK - FACT PACK (Far East Holdings Berhad). Regional Senior Manager En. Musa Bin Abdul Halim; Estate Manager En. Mohd Khairul Nizam Bin Zakaria (also oversees Ladang Rangkaian); Assistant Manager En. Mohd Ali Bin Hamid. Estate assets and vehicles are held under Ladang Rangkaian.

SOURCES. (1) PA Report 1/2026 (Planting Advisory), visit 29 June 2026, period reviewed January to May 2026, Planting Advisor Tn. Mohd Sufian Bin Yusoff; previous PA visit 19 November 2025 (PA 2/2025, period Jan-Oct 2025). Based on the May 2026 progress report. (2) Agronomy Report 1/2026, visit 20 April 2026, by En. Ghazali Bin Abd Ghani (Junior Agronomist) and Chong Kuan Ming (Senior Agronomist); previous agronomy visit 9 December 2025 (Agro 2/2025, which set the 2026 programme). Agro 1/2025 (12 June 2025) holds the 2025 programme.

AREA (PA 1/2026 Table 1, May 2026). Total 796.24 ha. Mature 640.30 ha: P18A 306.10 ha (148 SPH), P19B 193.90 ha (148), P20C 108.30 ha (127), P21D 32.00 ha (124); average 143 SPH; DxP Felda. Immature Field H (Delima) 24.10 ha (P08H replanted 2024-2025, managed by Ladang Delima). Conservation area 102.14 ha, tapping right 27.20 ha, forest tree 2.50 ha. Palms 5-8 years old (early mature); 60% of planted area is peat. Average rainfall about 3,500 mm over 120 days; heavy showers Nov-Jan. Agro 1/2026 census (GPS re-census for elephant damage) after supplying: P18A sub-blocks 141-148 SPH; P19B 148; P20C 147-148; P21D 147. 3,150 supply palms planted June 2025 in P20C (2,388) and P21D (762) all survived.

STAFF AND LABOUR (PA 1/2026, May 2026). 45 workers vs requirement 47 (1 worker per 14 ha): harvesting 24 (req 26), driver/loader 4 (3), weeding 5 (11), manuring 4 (4), mandor 1 (3), general worker 7 (0). 1 checkroll, 44 contract. 24 harvesters with 5 crawlers, 1 harvester per 27 ha, insufficient as crop rises. Contractors: Baharudin (harvesting and upkeep, all fields, 42 workers), Jas Ramai and Msr Idaman (driver/loader). In 5 months: 5 TKIs recruited, 10 returned home, 2 transferred out, 3 absconded.

CROP (PA 1/2026 Table 21, Jan-May 2026, 640.30 ha). FFB 4,399.00 t vs budget 4,080.00 t (+8%); same period 2025 4,148.20 t (+6%); annual budget 12,000 t; 2025 actual 11,255.92 t. Yield 6.87 t/ha vs budget 6.37 and 6.48 last year; annual budget 18.74 t/ha (Table 23 says 19.00). CPO 833.34 t, OER 18.94%; kernel 203.24 t, KER 4.62%; CPO 1.30 t/ha. Fruit set encouraging, many black bunches; on track for the annual target. Block Jan-May 2026: P18A 2,407.61 t, 7.87 t/ha, 6.44 bunches/palm, ABW 8.25 kg; P19B 1,334.97 t, 6.88 t/ha, 7.88 bunches, 5.90 kg; P20C 509.14 t, 4.70 t/ha, 6.12, 6.05 kg; P21D 147.28 t, 4.60 t/ha, 10.64, 3.49 kg. Estate 7.02 bunches/palm, ABW 6.83 kg. 2026 budgets t/ha: P18A 20.30, P19B 19.30, P20C 14.80, P21D 14.10.
Yield history (PA Table 23, t/ha): estate 2022 4.27, 2023 11.69, 2024 14.80, 2025 17.58. P18A 4.96, 13.78, 17.49, 20.43; P19B 3.18, 9.69, 14.67, 18.27; P20C -, 5.02, 8.48, 11.60; P21D 2025 6.93 (Agro: 3.14 in 2024, 6.39 in 2025). Agro 1/2026 App 2a tonnes: 2022 2,135.26; 2023 6,232.12; 2024 9,344.42 (monthly record 9,243.91); 2025 11,255.92. Monthly 2025: Jan 693.89, Feb 668.46, Mar 860.12, Apr 993.95, May 931.78, Jun 825.18, Jul 822.35, Aug 1,084.20, Sep 1,097.60, Oct 1,114.57, Nov 1,185.52, Dec 978.30. 2026: Jan 734.18, Feb 827.61, Mar 864.60 (Jan-Mar 2,426.39 t, 3.79 t/ha vs 3.47 in 2025, +9.2%). Agro: 2025 yield up 22% on 2024 (Table 13 shows 2024 as 15.59), young plantings still below potential; P21D 2025 below potential (expected 7-8 vs potential 11.9 t/ha) because of uneven growth, flooding and elephant damage at transplanting.

HARVESTING (PA 1/2026). Interval 15 days average, 10.00 rounds Jan-May 2026. Productivity 2.17 t/manday (4,399.00 t, 2,023 mandays): P18A 2.19, P19B 2.79, P20C 1.46, P21D 1.53. Rates RM45.00/t P18A, RM55.00 P19B, RM65.00 P20C, RM85.00 P21D; earnings RM94.99 to RM153.45 per day. Keep MRS of 1 fresh loose fruit to avoid unripe bunches; stack fronds so they do not block crawlers. 5 crawlers with 18 harvesters cover 608.30 ha (not P21D or poorly accessible low-lying areas): 7.15 t/machine-day, 2.17 t/harvester-day, a bit low. Agro 1/2026: intervals Jan-Mar 2026 15-17 to 15-19 days, slightly over 15 days; 2 harvesters short; 6 rounds to March; no overripe bunches or backlog in A1, A2, B2, C3; 24 rounds in 2025.

COST (PA 1/2026 Table 25, Jan-May 2026, RM per t FFB). General charges 87.88 vs budget 121.75 (annual 99.35); upkeep and cultivation 196.18 vs 195.80 (159.77); harvesting and collection 109.36 vs 145.21 (118.49); total ex-estate 393.42 vs 462.76 (annual 377.61), 15% below budget. Per t CPO 2,076.76 vs 2,565.31. Harvesting RM78.34/t (budget 95.16), internal transport 30.23 (43.44), supervision 0.79 (6.59). General charges RM401,139.95 = RM603.76/ha vs RM775.68 budget (24% under); overspent items: executive vehicle running RM5.46/ha (+20%, Hilux repairs, replaced April 2026), EPF labour RM15.81/ha (+35%), paid leave/VLP RM46.58 (+52%), medical/VMO RM7.62 (+53%), SRA RM4.45 (+108%), upkeep labour quarters RM27.24 (+59%, includes rent of mill worker quarters), entertainment RM8.39 (+43%), MSPO RM7.22 (+16%). Upkeep RM862,879 = RM1,347.77/ha vs RM1,247.63: weeding 111.98 (budget 123.05), manuring 897.62 (728.55, +23% fertiliser price), pest and disease 45.16 (57.11), census and thinning 3.19 (8.66), drains 57.48 (42.79), roads and bridges 121.35 (138.63), soil and water conservation 66.15 (79.72), boundaries 4.51 per text, pruning 40.34 (51.23). No capital expenditure; vehicles reported under Rangkaian. PA 2/2025 (Jan-Oct 2025): ex-estate RM337.58/t vs budget 397.27.

MANURING. PA 1/2026 Table 10 (H1 2026): Jan Mix B 82.55 t, Feb Mix B 145.15 t, Mar RP 178.20 t, Apr Mix B 81.45 t all completed; May Mix B 106.90 t not delivered; 487.35 of 594.25 t (82%). H2: Jul Mix B 142.30, Aug 57.40, Sep 130.95, Oct 57.40 = 388.05 t. Follow up supplier. Semi-mechanised Timac application 25 bags/manday, RM70-75/day. Agro 1/2026 (data to Apr): 230.70 t applied, 39% of H1, 23% of 982.30 t year; 2025 programme 723.80 t fully applied (Mix B 506.65, NK 2 80.20, RP 136.95). New fertiliser store in use. RP check in A5/A6: 1.5 kg/palm, 40 bags/day, acceptable. EFB Jan-May 2026: 286.90 mt on 8.98 ha (programme 10,000 mt); EFB 2025 5,258.92 mt on 171.36 ha; fertiliser cut not advised. 2026 programme (revised, Agro 1/2026 App 1, kg/palm): P18A Mix B 2.25 (Jan A1/A2/A4, Feb others), RP 1.75 Mar, Mix B 2.00 (Apr or May), Mix B 1.50 Jul and Sep; P19B Mix B 2.00 Feb, RP 2.00 Mar, Mix B 2.00 May, 1.50 Aug and Oct; P20C Mix B 1.75 Jan, RP 2.00 Mar, Mix B 2.00 Apr, 1.50 Jul and Sep; P21D Mix B 1.75 Jan, RP 2.00 Mar, Mix B 1.75 Apr, 1.50 Jul and Sep. Original Agro 2/2025 second-half rates were 2.25/2.00 (P18A), 2.00 (P19B, P20C), 1.75 (P21D). Supply palms half dose, RP 2 kg. Mix B = 45% AS, 40% MOP, 14% kieserite, 1% borate.

WEEDING (PA 1/2026). Circle spraying 964.60 of 1,280.60 ha to date (75%); selective 1,060.70 ha (83%); P21D both rounds done, P20C selective done. Productivity circle 4.50 ha/manday (CDA), selective 4.00 (mist blower), RM72/day. Limit glyphosate circles to 2 m; bare ground and surface runoff in all fields; low-lying waterlogged areas disrupt spraying. Agro 1/2026 (Mar 2026): inter-row round 1 P18A 100%, P19B 79%, P20C and P21D 100%; circle P18A 84%, P19B 79%, others 100%; ground cover acceptable, soft grasses dominant; B1 over-spraying improved. 2025 circle weeding 97%.

PESTS (both reports). Rat damage census Mar 2026: P18A 27%, P19B 32%, P20C 29%, P21D 26% (2025: Mar 42-45%, Sep 21-24%). PA: 1 round ARAKUS brodifacoum Jan-Apr 2026 on all fields; Agro: Storm flocoumafen baiting from April to end-May, census after one month. Barn owls 39 boxes (42 required), 1 per 16 ha, 29 occupied 74% (PA); 31 occupied 79% (Agro Mar 2026); Nov 2025 46%. Predator plants mainly Turnera; add Cassia cobanensis and Antigonon. Bagworm census Mar 2026: P18A 8, P19B 27, P20C 9; Altacor sprayed 210.89 ha; under control; post census required. Elephants: intrusion reduced after electric fence and patrols; still pulling fronds along roadsides near boundaries.

OTHER FIELD WORK (PA 1/2026). Palm census complete; thinning out ongoing; supplying in P20C and P21D completed, density should show in area statement. Drains: 676 chains desilted (main drain 8x6x4 18 chains, 5x4x3 658 chains), focus on 200 ha flood-prone area. Roads: 2,100 chains graded, 15 chains laterited; patch potholes, remove stagnant water. Soil mounding 2,586 palms (2,856 in 6.7.1) in P18A and P19B peat, target 10,000 this year. Boundary drain 65 chains desilted; boundaries good; do not leave bunches or fertiliser bags overnight at boundary. Pruning: progressive, 640.30 ha done; keep 2 fronds below lowest bunch; stack fronds among four palms. Agro: first pruning round completed March 2026; pruning and sanitation good in all sub-blocks.

LEAF NUTRIENTS (Agro 2/2025 foliar results, 2025). K deficient in all P19B sub-blocks (0.86-0.96%) and C1-C3 (0.94-0.98%); P18A K normal. N marginally low in A3, B1, B3, C2, C3. P marginally low in A1, A4 and P19B. Mg high in most. Cu and Zn marginal in some. Apr 2026: mild Mg and K symptoms in A3, A4, C1 and D. Water table in peat to be kept at 50-75 cm. Next sampling 2026 for the 2027 programme.

RAINFALL (mm, days). 2021 2,702 (118); 2022 3,844 (130); 2023 5,062.4 (117); 2024 3,481.6 (119); 2025 3,919.0 (139); Jan-May 2026 886.0 mm over 36 days (Jan 57, Feb 356, Mar 108, Apr 102, May 263).

CONCLUSIONS. PA: overall performance satisfactory; FFB above budget and cost below budget; continue pest control and drainage; supplying done. Agro: agronomic condition acceptable, no significant delays; rat and bagworm infestations need immediate attention; keep drains maintained for wet-season high water tables.
